stem: A donor planned for propagation shows new pest-like stippling. What should happen before cuttings are distributed?
choices: Hold or flag the donor material and follow the defined plant-health and biosecurity process before distributing cuttings.
Take the scheduled cuttings first and quarantine the rooted trays later if the donor symptoms progress.
Move the donor into the clean propagation area so symptoms can be compared under the same environment as healthy stock.
Use dedicated tools on the suspect donor, then distribute cuttings if no pest is visible on the harvested material.
rationale: A donor with new pest-like stippling can transfer a plant-health problem into many downstream propagules. The donor should therefore be held or flagged and evaluated through the defined plant-health and biosecurity process before cuttings are distributed. Propagating first creates a multiplication pathway, while moving the donor into clean space or relying only on visible pests weakens containment.
